## Session note: the entrance used as a holder would use it, at `0a32442eb091b7d6153a60fa869ca9384a9b1e39`

**Charter.** Use this repository's entrance as the holder of tradecraft #727 would: find where the change stands, what comes next, who owns that step and the exact command. Stop at the command if it would write to GitHub.
- The job named #727 and its pull request #736. It did not name this change or anything about it.
- #736 was the only other open change. It was chosen because it has a real record at the late stages this change rewrites: floor, use, reviewers and release.
- **The steer, recorded here and not given to the consumer:** a change at that point meets the new proof step and the gate's identification.
- **Time-box:** one turn of up to 3600 seconds. It used 9 minutes of wall time (23:38:32Z to 23:47:21Z).

**Consumer and tree.**
- **Consumer:** a fresh Claude seat launched by the installed 0.152.0 entrance's `run use` through `lib/dispatch_seat.py`. It ran cold with execute capability, and cross-vendor to the Codex builder, so staffing was `qualified`.
- **Model:** the 0.152.0 `opus` alias resolved to `claude-opus-5` at `max`. This change's Opus 5.5 default applies only once it ships.
- **Dispatch and cost:** `576a3e5820634cc09675bfd7eade33d5`, $2.61 (costUSD).
- **Tree:** repository-session mode, from `0a32442`.
  - Carried: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `skills/`, `lib/` without `lib/tests`, `.claude-plugin/`, `.tradecraft/`, `docs/values.md` and `docs/cells/steward/`, as one neutral detached commit.
  - Left out: the decision entry, because `docs/architecture/` wasn't carried.
  - A first build of the tree was discarded because its `lib/tests` exclusion didn't apply. `--exclude-record lib/tests` was recorded but left the files in; `lib/tests/**` removed them.
- **Residue carried:**
  - two code comments on the model defaults naming #731 and D-733;
  - the shipped cells' own prose about experience sessions.
  - #727's live record, which the job needed, mentions #725 as the place its launcher defect was seen.
- **Bodies-only:** no `.claude/` loading surface was carried, so the consumer reached cells by following the root instructions.
- **My checks before dispatch:** I ran the entrance on #727 in the tree myself and confirmed it answered from producer 0.153.0. That run left a `lib/__pycache__/` in the tree, which I removed before dispatch so the tree was clean again.

**What the run lived.**
- The consumer read inward from `CLAUDE.md` to `AGENTS.md`, the charter, the `work` cell, the marker reference and `proof.md`, then ran the ordinary entrance on #727. It answered `artifact-cap`, `artifact-cold-round-cap-reached`, holder-owned, dispatching nothing.
- The consumer distrusted that answer: the same report's 23 lawful markers showed a settled artifact, a build, two floors, two uses and three completed connected reviewers, all after the cap.
- It read #727 and #736 and the governing doctrine. `cold-seat.md`'s third settlement route, an owner ruling at the cap, matched #727's record exactly.
- It then recomputed the state with the entrance's own helpers (`read_state`, `prepare_use_evidence`, `set_proof_freshness`) without altering them, and reached `proof`, `current-head-proof-absent-or-outdated`.
- It stopped at the exact command, `run proof`, because that writes twice to GitHub: it posts the proof comment and requests the gate rerun. It named the holder as owner, because `run proof` launches nobody and needs no holder session.

**What worked, and why.**
- **`proof.md` stated the write behaviour exactly,** so the consumer knew where to stop without running anything.
- **The entrance's gate identification and evidence gathering were rich enough to reason from.** The consumer found, without being told, that #736's proof gate was green only because a rerun had nothing to read: no proof document existed at the head.
- **Its answer is the one this change is meant to produce** for a change in #736's state.

**Friction, as lived.**
- **The entrance's recommendation was wrong, and it looked authoritative.**
  - `artifact-cap` is returned before the artifact-status check. Past that branch, only a `would` cold verdict advances.
  - So an artifact settled by an owner ruling at the cap, or a `not settleable` discharged by revision, has no representation, and a change settled that way sits at `artifact-cap` indefinitely.
  - **This change didn't cause it.** The installed 0.152.0 entrance returns the same `artifact-cap` for #727 (checked by the holder). It's outside #725's brief and goes to the Steward as a fact.
- **The front page's `python tools/dev.py setup` doesn't exist in this tree,** which the job had told it.
- The consumer named a probe file `inspect.py`, shadowing the standard library. That cost it time, and it was its own.

**Where the consumer was itself wrong, or went beyond the job.** It went behind the entrance's answer by recomputing the decision with the entrance's helpers. It said the instructions didn't license that, and that it had to decide on its own whether verifying the answer was in scope. That judgement is the finding: a holder handed a stale non-command has nothing in the material telling it to distrust the entrance.

**What it consulted beyond the tree.** GitHub reads for #727 and #736 only: comments, review comments, reviews, files, one check run and one workflow run. It wrote a probe script in its own scratchpad, outside the tree. It posted nothing and committed nothing (`changed=false`).

**Not performed.** `run proof` on #727, as the job put it out of scope.

> **In plain terms:** getting a finished change through the gate used to stall on things that had nothing to do with the change:
> - a note posted where the gate doesn't read;
> - a marker naming an older head;
> - a label nobody knew to add;
> - two runs sharing one check name.
>
> With this change the entrance writes one proof document per head from the record, and the holder posts it with one command, `run proof`. The ready step adds the label the repository's configuration names. At release, `run release-report` names the required gate's result at the head, and says when the path-departures paragraph must record a bypass. The gate's half, which checks the proof document, lives in change-proof #20. The change also sets the practice's standing model defaults: Sol 5.6 for Codex, and Opus 5.5 for Claude. The owner chose them after the comparison on #731.

Closes #725
Closes #706
Closes #719
Closes #682
Closes #712

Refs change-proof#20 (the gate half), change-proof#17 and change-proof#18 (row 5: they land first, on their own), #731 (the comparison row 6 rests on), #737 (the comparison runs still owed)

**Waiting on you:** the merge. Everything the path owes has run at `0a32442eb091b7d6153a60fa869ca9384a9b1e39`, and the required gate is green there.

## What landed (head `0a32442`)

- **Proof composition and publication.**
  - A new `lib/proof.py` and a holder-owned `run proof` stage compose a version-1 proof document from the record, and post it to the pull request, one per head.
  - The shipped contract is `skills/work/references/proof.md` and `proof-v1.schema.json`, with positive and negative fixtures.
- **Ready step.** `run ready-reviewers` applies the label the work configuration names (`reviewer_label`, set to `reviewers` here), then marks the pull request ready. It confirms the head didn't move before and after the transition.
- **Evidence handling in the entrance:**
  - the ancestor-head rule for use evidence;
  - the generated no-use carrier;
  - check runs identified beyond their name;
  - a confirmed merge conflict named as the reason no runs exist, while an unknown mergeability isn't called one;
  - release recommended only on an explicit gate success.
- **The gate's result at release**, a row the owner added on [#725](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/725#issuecomment-5804459089).
  - `run release-report` reports `required_gate` at the current head: `green`, `red`, `stale` or `absent`, with the runs it read.
  - Where the result isn't green, it tells the holder to restate the `**Path departures:**` paragraph at that head, recording the bypass and its reason.
  - It records a bypass and doesn't forbid it, because merging is the owner's decision.
  - The guidance is in `skills/work/SKILL.md` and `skills/engagement/references/change-paths.md`.
- **Row 6: the owner's standing defaults**, pinned as full ids and marked interim.
  - `gpt-5.6-sol` at `xhigh` for the Codex implementer and Codex seats.
  - `claude-opus-5-5` at `high` for ordinary Claude seats, and at `max` for cold and terminal seats.
  - Under #731's rules every candidate came out inconclusive ([results](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/731#issuecomment-5804291939)). The owner chose these values ([Claude](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/725#issuecomment-5801169378), [Codex](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/725#issuecomment-5804269705)).
  - `skills/engagement/references/dispatch-records.md` carries the three-outcome rule, and the shipped roster says `high` for ordinary seats.
  - The runs still owed are #737: a three-way build of Sol 5.6, Sol 6 and Luna 6 from Astra-written artifacts, and a Claude judging run at `high`.
- **Experience-consumer effort.** `skills/engagement/references/the-stretch.md` now matches the code and the owner's ruling: the consumer runs cold, at `max`.
- **Decision entry:** `docs/architecture/decisions/D-733-2026-09-23-proof-as-one-act-per-head.md`.
- **Version:** plugin 0.153.0.

## Release proof at `0a32442`

- **Floor:** passed at `0a32442`, with lint clean and 1030 passed, 1 skipped ([floor note](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/pull/733#issuecomment-5804738722), bundle `20260923T233129Z-Grimblaz-and-Friends-tradecraft-725-floor-bee7e6f5e53f`).
- **CI:** `lint-and-test` green on Ubuntu and Windows.
- **Connected reviewers:** CodeRabbit, Greptile and the Codex connector all completed. Every thread has a disposition reply and is resolved.
- **Use:** passed at `0a32442`, staffing qualified, `changed=false` ([session note](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/pull/733#issuecomment-5804853547)). It found an entrance defect that predates this change: the ordinary decision misreports an artifact settled at the cap. That is #734, which now carries the note ([correction](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/pull/733#issuecomment-5804875944)).
- **Required gate:** `Change proof (required)` is green at `0a32442` ([run 35933901114](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/actions/runs/35933901114), job 107431362687). This change's own `run release-report` (0.153.0) read it as `verdict: green`, `restate: false`.
- **Panel:** not bought.

**Path departures:** This paragraph is written at `0a32442eb091b7d6153a60fa869ca9384a9b1e39`, the head that merges. A later head needs a fresh `run release-report` read.
- **Required gate:** green at that head, so no gate bypass is recorded.
- **Stalled: two hand-run resumes.** The launcher recorded the builder's completed turns for the build (`5d793f8`) and the first repair round as errors (#727). The entrance couldn't resume from those bundles, so the owner ran two resumes by hand with `dispatch_implementer.py --resume`: the first repair round and the floor at `6ca2e8c`. That floor was the first bundle recorded as a success. From then on, the second and third repair rounds, the floor at `0a32442` and the use all ran through the entrance.
- **The artifact** was chosen from #731's ten-arm comparison, as #725's protocol set out, and settled by a cross-vendor cold seat. The affirmed brief was re-posted unchanged ([comment 5793803434](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/725#issuecomment-5793803434)), because the winning artifact quoted the brief's marker and the entrance took it for the newest brief.
- **Row 6 departs from the brief's named interim** (Sol 6 at `xhigh`, and ordinary Claude seats at `xhigh`) by the owner's two rulings linked above.
- **The owner's added row** was built in the third repair round without a revised pre-implementation artifact or a fresh cold settle. [His ruling](https://github.com/Grimblaz-and-Friends/tradecraft/issues/725#issuecomment-5804459089) authorizes that.
- **Skipped: `run proof` on this pull request.** The installed entrance is 0.152.0, whose path doesn't include it, and the gate half that reads the proof document (change-proof #20) hasn't landed. The gate evaluated the existing floor and use markers.
- **Gate re-run by hand.** The change-proof gate re-ran through a job rerun after the use note, because posting a note doesn't trigger it.
- **The use consumer ran as `claude-opus-5` at `max`,** the 0.152.0 alias's resolution. This change's Opus 5.5 default applies only once it ships.
